Your task is to recreate a program from scratch based only on its observable behavior and bundled documentation.

Your submission must be an independent implementation.

## What is NOT allowed

### 1. Using an existing implementation

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the reference executable

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The reference `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the reference executable (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that only runs `chmod +x ./executable` or copies the reference executable (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. How the reference executable may be observed

All information about the reference `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the reference `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace

# i3-style

Make your i3 config a little more stylish.

About

i3-style applies a theme to your i3 config file to change the colorscheme of window decorations and the different parts of i3bar. It is designed especially for people who frequently change colorschemes.

- Easy to try out new themes.
- Themes are easy to read, modify, and share.
- Modifies your theme in place; templates are not required.

Usage

Call the tool with the name of the theme (or a path to a theme file) and the output location. The tool will apply the theme to your i3 configuration.

Example:

    i3-style solarized -o ~/.config/i3/config --reload

Or apply a theme file directly:

    i3-style ~/.config/i3/solarized.yaml -o ~/.config/i3/config

Send us themes!

If you have a colorscheme you'd like to share, you can convert an existing i3 config to a theme file:

    i3-style --to-theme ~/.config/i3/config -o my-theme.yaml

Please consider contributing new themes.

import subprocess,os
def run_apply(config_text, theme, extra=[]):

    try: os.unlink("/tmp/i3calls.log")
    except: pass
    p=subprocess.run(["./executable","-c","/tmp/cfg"]+extra+[theme] if False else ["./executable","-c","/tmp/cfg",theme]+extra, capture_output=True, text=True, env=env)
    log=""
    try: log=open("/tmp/i3calls.log").read()
    except: pass
    return p,log

# Test config templating variants
tests=[
 ("empty",""),
 ("no newline","font x"),
 ("only newline","\n"),
 ("no bar","font x\nbindsym y\n"),
 ("bar empty inline","bar {}\n"),
 ("bar empty multiline","bar {\n}\n"),
 ("bar with status","bar {\n status_command i3status\n}\n"),
 ("bar with colors existing","bar {\n colors {\n  background #111111\n }\n}\n"),
 ("bar with colors inline?","bar { colors { background #111111 } }\n"),
 ("multiple bars","bar {\n}\nbar {\n}\n"),
 ("client lines existing","client.focused #111111 #222222 #333333 #444444\nclient.unfocused #111111 #222222 #333333\nfont x\n"),
 ("client with extra spaces/tabs","  client.focused   #111111   #222222\n\tclient.urgent #1 #2 #3 #4 #5\n"),
 ("client placeholder?","client.placeholder #1 #2 #3 #4\nclient.background #111111\n"),
 ("commented client","# client.focused #111111 #222222 #333333 #444444\n"),
 ("bar colors commented?","bar {\n # colors {\n # }\n}\n"),
 ("nested bar?","bar {\n  bar {\n  }\n}\n"), # weird
]
for name,cfg in tests:
    p,log=run_apply(cfg,"solarized")
    print(f"=== {name} code={p.returncode} stderr={p.stderr!r} log={log!r}")
    print(repr(p.stdout))
    print(p.stdout)
    print("---end---")

use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::fmt;

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub enum Yaml {
    Null,
    Bool(bool),
    Int(i64),
    Real(String),
    Str(String),
    Array(Vec<Yaml>),
    Hash(Vec<(Yaml, Yaml)>),
}

impl Yaml {
    pub fn as_str(&self) -> Option<&str> {
        if let Yaml::Str(s) = self { Some(s) } else { None }
    }
    pub fn as_hash(&self) -> Option<&Vec<(Yaml, Yaml)>> {
        if let Yaml::Hash(h) = self { Some(h) } else { None }
    }
    pub fn lookup<'a>(&'a self, key: &str) -> Option<&'a Yaml> {
        if let Yaml::Hash(h) = self {
            for (k, v) in h {
                if let Yaml::Str(s) = k {
                    if s == key { return Some(v); }
                }
            }
        }
        None
    }
}

pub fn lookup<'a>(y: Option<&'a Yaml>, key: &str) -> Option<&'a Yaml> {
    y.and_then(|v| v.lookup(key))
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct Marker { pub index: usize, pub line: usize, pub col: usize }

#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct ScanError { pub mark: Marker, pub info: String }

impl ScanError {
    fn new(src: &str, byte_index: usize, info: &str) -> Self {
        let mut line = 1usize;
        let mut col = 0usize;
        for (i, ch) in src.char_indices() {
            if i >= byte_index { break; }
            if ch == '\n' { line += 1; col = 0; } else { col += 1; }
        }
        // If byte_index is in middle / at end after last char handling above is approximate.
        if byte_index > 0 && byte_index >= src.len() {
            // compute properly for end
            line = 1; col = 0;
            for ch in src.chars() {
                if ch == '\n' { line += 1; col = 0; } else { col += 1; }
            }
        }
        ScanError { mark: Marker { index: byte_index, line, col }, info: info.to_string() }
    }
}

// We intentionally format this to look like yaml-rust's ScanError debug form,
// because main prints it with {:?} in a panic message.
impl fmt::Debug for Marker {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        // Not used because ScanError has manual Debug below.
        write!(f, "Marker {{ index: {}, line: {}, col: {} }}", self.index, self.line, self.col)
    }
}

// Manual Debug for ScanError to match: ScanError { mark: Marker { index: X, line: Y, col: Z }, info: "..." }
// Note derive would also do same if fields named same, but Marker derive would conflict.

    items=data.items() if isinstance(data,dict) else [((r,g,b),n) for r,g,b,n in data]

        for n,c in centers:

pub fn get_name(hex: &str) -> String {
    let stripped = if let Some(s) = hex.strip_prefix('#') { s } else { hex };
    let chars: Vec<char> = stripped.chars().collect();
    if chars.len() < 6 {
        panic!("got invalid hex string: {:?}", hex);
    }
    let mut rgb = [0f64; 3];
    for i in 0..3 {
        let pair: String = chars[i*2..i*2+2].iter().collect();
        match u8::from_str_radix(&pair, 16) {
            Ok(v) => rgb[i] = v as f64,
            Err(_) => {
                panic!("got invalid hex string: {:?}", hex);
            }
        }
    }
    let mut best_name = COLORS[0].0;
    let mut best_dist = f64::INFINITY;
    for (name, (r, g, b)) in COLORS {
        let dr = rgb[0] - *r;
        let dg = rgb[1] - *g;
        let db = rgb[2] - *b;
        let d = dr*dr + dg*dg + db*db;
        if d < best_dist {
            best_dist = d;
            best_name = name;
        }
    }
    best_name.to_string()
}
